spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The decisive move is to replace a locally convergent zero cloud by a normalized microscopic analytic process: evaluate the characteristic polynomial at displacement z/n, divide by its value at 1, and couple all dimensions so the resulting functions can converge pathwise even though ordinary moments fail.

Virtual isometries provide an almost-sure cross-dimensional coupling; a moment method is obstructed because the rescaled function lacks even a first moment on the circle.

directed.boundary_or_failure: Local convergence of zero point processes alone does not determine the global infinite-product function. The random-matrix construction is proved here, whereas proposed consequences for zeta are not established by this motivation.

The scale choice is meant to retain zero-driven short-range structure while suppressing prime-driven long-range structure.

The zero-counting asymptotic N(T)=T/(2π) log(T/(2πe))+O(log T) motivates rescaling zeta ordinates to average spacing one; equality of their limiting correlations with the sine process is conjectural.

directed.representation_or_bridge: The sine-kernel point process is the bridge object; correlation functions are determinants of the rescaled kernel on the CUE side and are conjectured for rescaled zeta zeros.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The CUE point-process limit is stated as a theorem, but the zeta comparison is Montgomery/GUE-type conjecture. The span does not upgrade correlation agreement to convergence of analytic functions.
directed.uncertainty: Low for the normalization and evidentiary distinction; displayed kernel and scaling formulas carry ordinary extraction risk.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Dividing Z_n(e^{2πiz/n}) by Z_n(1) converts two individually nonconvergent nearby values into an order-one relative process. Treating all z at once preserves analytic structure and exposes more than a list of limiting zeros.

Finite collections of mutual characteristic-polynomial ratios become ratios of ξ_n values.

directed.representation_or_bridge: ξ_n is the intermediate representation between a finite characteristic polynomial and the limiting entire function; the compact-uniform topology preserves evaluation and differentiation.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The virtual-isometry construction turns unrelated Haar matrices into successive rank-one extensions on one probability space. This makes individual rescaled eigenangles trackable across n and supplies the pathwise spectral approximation needed for a functional limit.

The product consisting of the y_0 factor and paired positive/negative factors is absolutely convergent; compact-uniform limits make ξ_∞ entire, and the factors identify its zeros exactly as the y_k.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Compact-uniform holomorphic convergence is a high-leverage statement: it immediately transfers to finite products of ratios and, via derivative convergence, to rescaled derivatives. Passing expectations is deliberately left as a separate uniform-integrability problem.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For fixed numerator and denominator parameters, the microscopic characteristic-polynomial ratio converges almost surely to the corresponding ratio of ξ_∞ values when denominator points avoid the random zero set. spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: A zero-avoiding contour converts convergence of entire functions and their derivatives into convergence of consistently chosen logarithms. The imaginary part of that logarithm then becomes a spectral counting coordinate, so analytic phase records discrete eigenvalue counts.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The logarithm of Z_n is fixed by vanishing at zero on a slit domain. For a contour L avoiding zeros, log ξ_n(z)=∫_L ξ_n'/ξ_n, and compact-uniform convergence plus nonvanishing on L gives log ξ_n(z)→log ξ_∞(z). The identity N_n(z)=z-(1/π)Im log ξ_n(z) for real z yields convergence of microscopic arc counts to sine-process interval counts.

directed.representation_or_bridge: The zero-avoiding contour and logarithmic derivative bridge compact analytic convergence to logarithm branches; the argument principle bridges those branches to counting functions.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Differentiating the canonical product turns the entire function into a meromorphic resolvent: ξ_∞'/ξ_∞=iπ plus a symmetrically paired sum of 1/(z-y_k). This is the reusable analytic interface to the sine points.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Away from the real zero set, the rescaled logarithmic derivative of Z_n converges almost surely to ξ_∞'/ξ_∞. The latter equals iπ+1/(z-y_0)+∑_{k≥1}[1/(z-y_k)+1/(z-y_{-k})], and products of finite-n logarithmic derivatives converge to corresponding products of the limit.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The missing step from pathwise ratio convergence to computable ratio laws is uniform off-real integrability. Once supplied, expectation limits coexist with a determinantal identity, while the visually similar zeta formula remains explicitly conjectural.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: On compact subsets of C minus R, ratios ξ_n(z')/ξ_n(z) have pth moments uniformly over finite n and n=∞, so balanced products of ratios have finite expectations and their expectations converge uniformly. A randomized, microscopically shifted zeta-ratio limit with analogous half-plane factors is then conjectured.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The argument of the characteristic polynomial is a sawtooth spectral counter: it rises at deterministic speed along the circle and drops by π at each eigenvalue. Subtracting this phase variation from arc length yields an exact eigenvalue count and hence eigenangle-index error.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For nonzero endpoints A and B on the circle, the number of zeros on the counterclockwise arc equals n times arc length divided by 2π minus the change of Im log Z_n divided by π. Specializing just beyond the kth eigenangle gives an identity relating k, the rescaled eigenangle y_k^(n), and a difference of characteristic-polynomial arguments.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: A pointwise subgaussian estimate becomes a uniform circle estimate by combining rotational invariance on an n-point grid, Borel-Cantelli, and deterministic sawtooth interpolation between grid points.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: A Gamma-product formula for the moment generating function of Im log Z_n(1), followed by Chernoff optimization, gives probability at most 2 exp[-x²/(C+log n)]. Rotational invariance applies this bound to a regular n-point grid; summability for thresholds D log n with D>√2 and Borel-Cantelli give eventual grid control, and the argument's slope n/2 with downward π jumps fills the gaps to obtain a uniform O(log n) bound.

directed.representation_or_bridge: The regular grid is the discretization bridge, and Proposition 2.1 supplies deterministic interpolation between sampled phases.

The centered count has a Bernstein-type tail exp[-min(t²/(4 Var X_I),t/2)], and bounded exponential moments follow from the Bernoulli decomposition of determinantal counts. Fourier formulas for the two-point function supply the variance estimate.

For finite n, the argument bound gives y_k^(n)=k+O(log n), and in a small central window y_k^(n)=y_k+O(n^{-ε}). Splitting at about |k|=n^{1/7} patches these estimates into y_k^(n)=k+O(log(2+|k|)) uniformly in n and k.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Far resolvent tails are controlled by grouping the spectrum into growing positive and negative blocks. Deterministic mean contributions nearly cancel, while centered block-count fluctuations are handled by Jensen weights and determinantal exponential moments, uniformly for finite n and the limit.

This follows by choosing an exponential-moment parameter of order √A/log A, using x^p≲_p e^x, and controlling bounded residual windows by exponential moments of point counts. Consequently ξ_∞'/ξ_∞ has moments of every order, and joint moments equal limits of bounded-window sums.

Splitting equal and unequal point indices produces a diagonal one-point term and an off-diagonal term with density 1-S(y_1-y_2)^2; contour integration then resolves the half-plane dependence.
